questions.q: Why has warehousing been called 'transportation at zero miles per hour'?
o: Warehousing and transportation are substitutes for each other
Warehouses are always located next to highways
Products in a warehouse are always moving
questions.d: Warehousing stores products at and between points of origin and consumption. Warehousing and transportation are substitutes for each other, so warehousing has been called 'transportation at zero miles per hour'.

questions.q: What is the key reason for warehousing?
o: Patterns of production and consumption do not coincide
Transportation is always more expensive than storage
Customers prefer to collect goods from warehouses
Governments require goods to be stored before sale
questions.d: The key reason for warehousing is that patterns of production and consumption do not coincide. Warehousing matches different rates or volumes of flow.

questions.q: A wholesaler receives full pallets of rice and splits them into smaller cartons for small shops. Which regrouping function is this?
questions.d: Regrouping takes four forms. Accumulating (bulk making): bringing together similar stocks from different sources. Allocating (bulk breaking): breaking larger quantities into smaller ones. Assorting: building a variety of products for particular customers. Sorting out: separating products into grades and qualities.

questions.q: Separating products into the grades and qualities wanted by different target markets is called:
questions.d: Sorting out means separating products into grades and qualities desired by different target markets. Assorting means building up a variety of different products for resale to particular customers.

questions.q: Which type of facility mainly tries to maximise throughput?
questions.d: Warehouses emphasise storage and try to maximise use of storage space. Distribution centres emphasise rapid movement and try to maximise throughput: the amount of product entering and leaving a facility in a given time.

questions.q: What distinguishes a cross-docking facility from a distribution centre?
o: How long product stays in the facility: 24 hours or less for cross-docking
Cross-docking facilities store products for months
Cross-docking facilities are always publicly owned
questions.d: Cross-docking means receiving product and shipping it out the same day or overnight without putting it into storage. It differs from a distribution centre by the length of time product is in the facility (24 hours or less).

questions.q: Which design is recommended for a cross-docking facility?
o: Minimal storage space and truck doors on two or more sides
Maximum storage space and a single loading door
High racking to use the full cubic capacity
No truck doors, using conveyors only
questions.d: Cross-dock facilities should be designed with a minimal amount of storage space and truck doors on two or more sides. Designs include 'H', 'I', 'T', 'U' and 'E' configurations.

questions.q: Which type of warehousing is used most by retail chain stores?
questions.d: Private warehousing is owned by the firm storing goods there. It generates high fixed costs and suits companies with large volumes; its largest users are retail chain stores.

questions.q: Which of these is a drawback of PRIVATE warehousing?
o: It is less attractive when interest rates are high
Lack of control by the user
Users must rent space month to month
questions.d: Private warehousing drawbacks: high fixed cost, the need for high and steady demand volumes, being less attractive when interest rates are high, and reduced flexibility. Lack of control is a drawback of public warehousing.

questions.q: How does contract warehousing compare on cost?
o: Less costly than private warehousing and more costly than public warehousing
The same cost as public warehousing
questions.d: Contract (third-party or dedicated) warehousing is less costly than private warehousing and more costly than public warehousing, and offers more value-adding services than public warehousing.

questions.q: Which type of warehousing is bought through contracts of at least one year and suits smaller organisations without enough volume for their own facility?
questions.d: Multi-client warehousing mixes attributes of contract and public warehouses. Services are bought through minimum one-year contracts and suit smaller organisations that cannot build their own facilities or use one-client contract warehousing.

questions.q: Compared with other types, multi-client warehousing services are:
o: More differentiated than public, but less customised than contract
questions.d: Multi-client warehousing services are more differentiated than those in a public facility and less customised than those in a contract facility.

questions.q: How should a facility with LOW rates of product turnover be laid out?
o: To maximise use of the facility's cubic capacity
To speed the flow of product in and out
With truck doors on all four sides
questions.d: A facility with low turnover should maximise utilisation of its cubic capacity. A facility emphasising rapid movement should be configured to facilitate the flow of product into and out of it.

questions.q: In a variable slot location system:
o: Empty slots are assigned to incoming products based on space availability
Each SKU has one or more permanent slots
Slots are assigned by product price
questions.d: In fixed slot locations each SKU has one or more permanent slots. In variable slot locations, empty slots are assigned to incoming products based on space availability.

questions.q: According to the general rule of thumb, which is cheaper?
o: Building up (vertical) rather than building out (horizontal)
Building out (horizontal) rather than building up (vertical)
Renting is always cheaper than building
questions.d: The general rule of thumb is that it is cheaper to build up than to build out.

questions.q: Approximately what share of a facility's cubic capacity is actually occupied by product?
questions.d: Only about 10 percent of a facility's cubic capacity is actually occupied by product. Space is also needed for washrooms, lunchrooms, offices, hazardous-item storage, supplies and more.

questions.q: Public warehouses require a capital investment from the user.
questions.d: Public warehouses require no capital investment by the user, who rents space as needed, often month to month.

questions.q: The fatality (accident) rate in warehousing is higher than the average rate for all industries.
questions.d: Warehouses, distribution centres and cross-docking facilities can be dangerous workplaces; the warehousing fatality rate is higher than the average for all industries.

questions.q: Contract warehousing is also called third-party (3PL) or dedicated warehousing, and the vendor and client share the risks.
questions.d: Contract warehousing is a long-term arrangement providing tailored services exclusively to one client, where the vendor and client share the risks.

questions.q: Warehouse productivity is measured as input divided by output.
questions.d: Productivity is a measure of output divided by input, e.g. cases, product lines or pallets shipped per person.
